content: Bicillin C-R is an injectable suspension that contains equal amounts of two salts of penicillin G: penicillin G benzathine and penicillin G procaine. This medication is specifically designed for deep intramuscular injection. Penicillin G benzathine is synthesized through a chemical reaction between dibenzylethylenediamine and two molecules of penicillin G. Its chemical name is (2S,5R,6R)-3,3-Dimethyl-7-oxo-6-(2-phenylacetamido)-4-thia-1-azabicycloheptane-2-carboxylic acid compound with N,N'-dibenzylethylenediamine (2:1), tetrahydrate. It appears as a white, crystalline powder that is minimally soluble in water and moderately soluble in alcohol. Penicillin G procaine, on the other hand, is an equimolar salt formed by the combination of procaine and penicillin G. Its chemical name is (2S,5R,6R)-3,3-Dimethyl-7-oxo-6-(2-phenylacetamido)-4-thia-1-azabicycloheptane-2-carboxylic acid compound with 2-(diethylamino)ethyl p-aminobenzoate (1:1) monohydrate. It appears as white crystals or a fine, white microcrystalline powder and is slightly soluble in water. Each 2 mL disposable syringe of Bicillin C-R contains a total of 1,200,000 units of penicillin G. This includes 600,000 units of penicillin G in the form of the benzathine salt and 600,000 units of penicillin G in the form of the procaine salt. The suspension is stabilized in an aqueous solution buffered with sodium citrate. Additionally, the formulation contains approximately 0.5% lecithin, 0.55% carboxymethylcellulose, 0.55% povidone, 0.1% methylparaben, and 0.01% propylparaben as weight/volume (w/v) components. The injectable suspension is viscous and opaque in appearance. It is essential to review the sections on contraindications, warnings, precautions, and dosage and administration before using this medication.
